newsitem.title: FRANCE: Belgian move does not block whole deal-Cacao Barry.
newsitem.headline: Belgian move does not block whole deal-Cacao Barry.

text.p: French cocoa processor Cacao Barry said on Friday a Belgian ruling against the planned merger of Cacao Barry and Callebaut AG did not block the deal as a whole as it only affected the Belgian elements.
"The main point is that this is not threatening the whole transaction," said Patrick Bendavid, joint chairman of the Barry group.
Belgium's anti-trust authority said earlier it ruled against the planned merger because it would reinforce Callebaut's dominant position and significantly hamper competition.
In August Callebaut chairman Charles Gebhard said the group was awaiting approval from cartel authorities in certain countries but the due diligence process was over.
Bendavid specified that the deal had already won approval from local cartel authorities in Italy and Germany and was awaiting approval from authorities in Britain.
He did not say what steps the company would take in the wake of the Belgian ban, adding it needed to fully review the ruling.

Callebaut AG announced in July it had agreed to acquire Cacao Barry from its main shareholder, French holding company Societe Centrale d'Investissements (SCIA), creating a group with control of 12 to 13 percent of the world cocoa bean crop.
SCIA is 51 percent owned by Societe Centrale d'Investissement and Belgian holding company Cie Nationale a Portfeuille.
Callebaut is a unit of Swiss diversified holding Klaus J. Jacobs, owned by Swiss financier Klaus Jacobs.
Chocolate industry representatives had warned when the merger plans were announced that Callebaut and Cacao Barry had a strong presence in Belgium, which could raise competition issues.
